title: Samurai Lifting Wisdom
summary: NH draws lessons for lifters from Miyamoto Musashi's Book of Five Rings: train for life, do not hasten the blooming of the flower, become your own teacher, and build knowledge from small things. He argues that training should be calm and part of everyday life, aimed at a clear goal, honest and broad-minded, with the way found in training rather than in theory.
claims: Musashi trained from 13 until his death; you will not stay in your physical prime forever, but anyone can stay active and physically dominant for life
Talent exists, but anyone who follows the way can surpass people who do not train; potential is not visible after two months, so keep training to reveal it
Refuse to be locked into one dogma; tunnel vision only helps if you happen to be heading in the right direction
Do not let a fitness teacher own you; learn from them, but you are your own best teacher, and a good teacher gives you wings rather than clipping them
There is no single best method: broad programming principles hold across the board, but there are many lanes within them and one will suit you best
Modern life has made men too soft; find a middle ground by deliberately bringing back discomfort
Do not hasten the blooming of the flower: pushing progression you cannot sustain leads to injury and usually comes from comparing yourself to others
He started training at 15 but really bloomed at 20-21; what matters is how the flower looks at the end, even if it takes 20 or 30 years
Immature strategy causes grief: many lifters never update their methods, so the limiting factor is their thinking more than their muscles or genetics
The modern world is designed to make you soft, so building muscle is a war that needs planning, and the danger today is an early spiritual death
Musashi's most repeated advice, you must train, is the most important; without practice everything else is useless
From one thing know 10,000 things: work out how to adapt programs yourself instead of asking, and accept being wrong in order to build judgment
People do not know which fitness source to believe because they never developed their own ability to test information
Treat training as an ordinary part of life rather than a hyped event; hype is unsustainable, and he cannot remember the last time he skipped a session
Start sessions calm and save your intensity for when you have to push the weight; you can only unleash the beast if you are calm the rest of the time
Choose your destination and regularly ask why you are training; months of training without a purpose lead to disappointment and wasted energy
When you see lifting in everything around you, it has become part of your identity and you will not quit
Do not copy YouTubers' paths: theirs is not yours, they are far ahead of you, and they often make you feel you will never catch up
The background of training, meaning recovery, diet, social life and what you study, has its own timing, and a good action at the wrong time fails
Lifting is an intellectual pursuit for him; he trains two to three hours a day, and the thinking he does outside the gym is what keeps him going
Let your mind broaden as your frame does; tunnel vision makes you ignore good options that could replace bad ones in your arsenal
Do not even think dishonestly; dishonest thoughts produce excuses for slowing down and giving up
The way is in training: all the theory exists only to be applied, and the doing matters more than the thinking
Name your gains and losses objectively; hours on Instagram or porn are useless and toxic, while an hour of TV with family can be legitimate recovery
All programming knowledge originally came from people working it out with their bodies; reading without training gives no gains
Both an elevated spirit and a low spirit are weak because neither can be sustained
Musashi's posture, with shoulders lowered, buttocks not sticking out, legs braced from knee to toes and abdomen braced, is essentially the ideal lifting position for a neutral spine
Most modern people stand relying on tendons and passive structures instead of muscles, which leads to spine and knee problems
Use a two-fold gaze: broad perception plus focused sight, switching between them in training and life
Self-improvement puts you at the centre; teachers who make it about themselves, as much of YouTube fitness does, corrupt it
